title: Captions on a track, not in the picture
statement: Give a teaching film switchable captions on a separate track, never burned into the picture, keep a transcript, and keep on-screen text to the labels that teach.
detail: A video design reference rejected subtitles and full narrated text burned into the teaching visual, while the lesson player required accessible captions and a printed home for spoken teaching. The course reconciled the two by giving captions and a transcript their own selectable track and keeping the main visual to useful labels and diagrams, and the produced unit films were made this way. The record that sets this out calls it a reconciliation proposal, not a settled ruling.
against: "This is a reconciliation proposal, not a recovered academic ruling." (grade3-reading/visual-findings-2026-09-07/review-readiness/curriculum-alignment/rebuild/methodology/README.md:92)

evidence.quote: Use captions as a selectable accessibility track. Do not burn in every narrated sentence. Transcript must remain available.
Proposed implementation: provide a separate accessible caption/transcript track while keeping the main video visual to useful labels and diagrams.
Caption/transcript accessibility remains required; do not burn a competing word-by-word transcript over the teaching visual.
Provide an accessible caption track and transcript.
The video's main visual uses selective labels and relational diagrams; captions are a separate accessibility track.
